The database schema named "rschema_0339" consists of three tables: "project", "API", and "API_Response_Record".
The "project" table is used to store information about the projects. It has three columns: "Avatar_URL" which is a VARCHAR type and can store up to 255 characters, "Project_ID" which is an INTEGER type and is the primary key, and "Project_Name" which is also a VARCHAR type and can store up to 255 characters.
The "API" table is used to store information about the APIs. It has four columns: "Access_Path" which is a VARCHAR type and can store up to 255 characters, "Belonging_Project" which is an INTEGER type and cannot be null, "Identifier" which is an INTEGER type and is the primary key, and "Name" which is a VARCHAR type and can store up to 255 characters. The "Belonging_Project" column is a foreign key referencing the "Project_ID" in the "project" table.
The "API_Response_Record" table is used to store information about the API response records. It has four columns: "API_Identifier" which is an INTEGER type and cannot be null, "Call_Time" which is a DATETIME type, "Response_Time" which is also a DATETIME type, and both "API_Identifier" and "Call_Time" are the primary key. The "API_Identifier" column is a foreign key referencing the "Identifier" in the "API" table.
This schema ensures referential integrity by enforcing the constraints of foreign keys. When a record in the "project" table is deleted, any corresponding records in the "API" table will also be deleted due to the CASCADE delete rule. Similarly, when a record in the "API" table is deleted, any corresponding records in the "API_Response_Record" table will also be deleted due to the CASCADE delete rule.
gold_question: "The API performance management system is used to track and analyze the usage of various APIs across multiple projects. The system is required to record each project's ID, name, and related avatar information. Each project may contain multiple APIs, with each API bound to a project, and the system must record each API's unique identifier, name, and access path. To monitor the performance of the APIs, the system must collect statistics on each API's call frequency, average response time, and 90％ response time. Additionally, the system must record each API's creation and update times to track their development history. Users can view and analyze the performance data of APIs through the system to optimize the response efficiency of the APIs."

-- Schema for database: rschema_0339
CREATE TABLE `project` (
  `Project_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Project_Name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Avatar_URL` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Project_ID`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `API` (
  `Identifier` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Access_Path` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Belonging_Project` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Identifier`),
  CONSTRAINT `API_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`Belonging_Project`) REFERENCES `project` (`Project_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `API_Response_Record` (
  `API_Identifier` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Call_Time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `Response_Time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`API_Identifier`, `Call_Time`),
  CONSTRAINT `API_Response_Record_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`API_Identifier`) REFERENCES `API` (`Identifier`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
